instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.68(1) requires every principal registered under § 13.64 to file an expense statement on specified dates.
The statute mandates filing 'on or before July 31 and January 31' covering the preceding 6-month reporting period, i.e., semiannual reporting.
The reporting deadlines are twice per year (July 31 and January 31), not once annually.
No quarterly filing cadence is specified; instead, the statute specifies semiannual filings.
The statute does not require monthly expense statements, only filings due July 31 and January 31.
Nothing in § 13.68(1) provides for three-times-per-year reporting; it requires twice yearly reporting.
Section 13.68(1) specifies a single cadence (semiannual) and does not authorize or require any other periodic schedule.
The expense statement must include 'the aggregate total amount of lobbying expenditures made and obligations incurred' for lobbying by the principal and its lobbyists.
The aggregate total must include compensation to lobbyists and, when amounts to any lobbyist exceed $200, the lobbyist's name/address and total paid must be listed.

If payments to any lobbyist exceed $200 in the reporting period, the statement must list the lobbyist's name and address and total amount paid, thereby listing lobbyists employed (at least above the threshold).
The statute requires that the 'name ... of the lobbyist' be listed when spending to that lobbyist exceeds $200 during the reporting period.
For any lobbyist with more than $200 in expenditures/obligations, the statement must list the lobbyist's 'address' along with the name.

The statement must report office overhead-type costs (office space, utilities, supplies, and compensation of employees used in preparing for lobbying) when the lobbyist is an employee/officer/director of the principal.
The required time record must include 'a daily itemization of the time' spent on specified lobbying-related activities.
The time record must itemize time spent 'meeting with elective state officials, agency officials, [and] legislative employees,' which captures lobbying contacts/meetings.

The statement must identify each legislative proposal, proposed administrative rule, budget bill subject, or other topic accounting for 10% or more of lobbying time and estimate the proportion of time for each, reflecting general issues/topics.

The expense statement must report time proportions for each 'legislative proposal' (i.e., a bill/resolution) and each 'proposed administrative rule number,' requiring identification tied to specific numbered measures.

The statement must list any officials/candidates reimbursed under § 13.621(7)(a) and the date and amount reimbursed, covering reimbursements for actual and reasonable expenses related to participation/presentation (a form of things of value/expenses).
Section 13.68(1) enumerates required contents (expenditures, time records, reimbursements, travel totals) but does not require listing the principal’s address/phone on the expense statement itself.
The expense statement content requirements in § 13.68(1) do not include a description of the principal’s business activity/nature (those appear in the registration statement under § 13.64(1)).
No provision in § 13.68 requires disclosure of contributors to the principal or other major financial supporters.

Principal registration must list partner/member names for partnerships/LLCs and, for associations, describe representation and provide the approximate number of members (member-related identification information required on the registration form).
